In the BRCA subset, using a normal-vs-skew-normal likelihood-ratio test on dependency-score distributions with BH-FDR < 0.05 in both cohorts, I found 1357 significant selective dependencies in TCGA patient-level predicted DepMap scores and 232 in BRCA cell lines, with 1191 genes significant in patients but not in cell-line models.

The strongest patient-specific BRCA dependencies/biomarkers by patient-selectivity significance were SOX10 (LRT 519.223, FDR 1.23e-111), PDCL3 (466.870, 1.51e-100), SOX9 (424.623, 1.58e-91), UGCG (423.532, 2.04e-91), SRPK1 (416.235, 6.33e-90), ASCL1 (402.907, 4.20e-87), FOXA2 (374.537, 4.73e-81), CDK4 (315.268, 3.39e-68), MYOD1 (314.696, 4.07e-68), and ZFAND5 (304.184, 7.21e-66). These genes were significant in BRCA patients but not in BRCA cell lines under the same threshold.

Among patient-specific genes with especially strong average predicted dependency (more negative mean score), notable examples were EIF1AX (-1.712), PSMB5 (-1.656), THAP1 (-1.522), COPG1 (-1.492), CCND1 (-1.228), HMGCS1 (-1.148), and ELL (-1.151). Genes with the largest patient-versus-cell-line dispersion gap included CCND1 (SSD 105.219 vs 10.883), TP53 (81.159 vs 3.766), CDK4 (52.497 vs 11.572), ACO2 (34.252 vs 6.256), EFR3A (26.657 vs 3.977), SOX9 (25.030 vs 2.592), and COPG1 (26.002 vs 4.960), supporting that these selective patterns are much more pronounced in patients than in the BRCA cell-line models.

Shared significant dependencies between patients and cell lines were much fewer (166 genes) and included FOXA1, TP63, GATA3, EGFR, and FANCG, while 66 genes were cell-line-specific. Overall, the BRCA patient predicted dependency landscape is substantially richer than what is captured by the available BRCA cell-line cohort, so relying on cell lines alone would miss many candidate BRCA vulnerabilities.

Important limitation: the TCGA dependency scores are predicted rather than experimentally measured, and the BRCA cell-line cohort is much smaller (36 usable lines vs 1099 patients), so these patient-specific hits should be interpreted as translational hypotheses for follow-up validation rather than definitive therapeutic targets.
